summary.text: A world line is the path an object traces through four-dimensional spacetime, made of the sequence of events in its history.
Each point on it is an event labeled by a time and a position, so Earth's yearly circle around the sun becomes a helix that never closes.
Hermann Minkowski pioneered the idea, and on a diagram the tilt of a line shows speed: vertical means at rest and more tilt means faster.

facts.label: Earth's world line
facts.value: A helix that never returns to the same point

facts.label: Extended objects
facts.value: Trace a world tube, not a world line

items.prompt: Earth returns each year to the same place relative to the sun. Why doesn't its world line close into a loop?

options.label: Its orbit is not really a circle
It arrives at that place at a later time
The sun's position never repeats
Orbits cannot be drawn in spacetime

items.explain: The place repeats but the time does not, so the world line spirals as a helix.

items.prompt: On a spacetime diagram with time running upward, what does a perfectly vertical line represent?

options.label: A particle at maximum speed
A rod lying across space
A particle at rest
A particle that is speeding up

items.explain: A line at constant space coordinate may represent a particle at rest or a stationary observer.

items.prompt: Two particles are drawn on one diagram. One line leans slightly from vertical and the other leans far more. Which particle is faster?

options.label: The one that leans more
The one that leans less
They are equally fast
It depends on the line's length

items.explain: The more a line is tilted from the vertical, the larger the speed.

items.prompt: Two world lines begin apart, then meet at a single event. What does that usually depict?

options.label: Two particles speeding up together
A particle decaying into two others
One particle at rest watching another
A collision or encounter

items.explain: Two world lines that start separately and intersect signify a collision or encounter.

items.prompt: A planet is treated as having real volume rather than as a point. What does it trace through spacetime?

options.label: A world sheet, like a string
A world tube
A single point
A straight null curve

items.explain: Once an object has extended volume it traces a world tube instead of a world line.

items.prompt: A horizontal line segment at constant time could represent a rod, yet it is not a proper world line. Why?

options.label: It traces only the rod's length, not a history
It would imply motion faster than light
It has no starting event to label
It cannot be drawn on a coordinate grid

items.explain: A proper world line traces the time history of a particle or observer, while a horizontal segment just traces length.
